questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to design a successful dating app that people want to use
Why marriages last longer today
How to find the perfect partner
What happens in our brains when we use dating apps
questions.why: Dan says they are looking at what our brains are doing when we use dating apps.

questions.q: What does Rob say about using dating apps?
options: He would never use one
He uses them every day
He met his partner on one
He is thinking of trying one
questions.why: Rob says 'No way, I would never use one.'

questions.q: According to Alice Gray, how is choosing a partner on an app different from meeting in person?
options: It takes much longer online
Online we choose more carefully
It is actually very similar in our brain
Our brains don't react at all online
questions.why: She says it's easy to think it would be very different, 'when actually it's really similar'.

questions.q: According to Dan, what happens once you swipe left on someone?
options: They get a message from you
You will never see them again
They can still ask to meet you
They appear again the next day
questions.why: Dan says once you've swiped left you will never see that person again.

questions.q: What advantage of meeting someone in real life does Dan point out?
options: You can get to know them and start to like them
It is much cheaper than paying to use a dating app
You never get rejected
You can meet more people
questions.why: Dan says you might not find someone attractive at first but then get to know and like them.

questions.q: According to Alice Gray, what is the main difference with rejection on dating apps?
options: It doesn't hurt at all
It hurts much more each time
It happens far more often
It only happens to men
questions.why: She says the patterns are similar, but the amount of rejection on dating apps is a lot higher.

questions.q: Why is rejection in real life easier to deal with, according to Alice Gray?
options: Friends are there to help you
You have time to recover before the next one
People are much kinder when they reject you face to face
You forget about it straight away
questions.why: She says in real life you have time to compute the rejection, get over it and dust yourself off.

questions.q: Why does Dan describe someone falling over on the ground?
options: To tell a funny story about a date
To warn about using phones while walking
To show how painful rejection is
To explain the idea of recovering and carrying on
questions.why: He explains 'dust yourself off' as getting up and making yourself ready again before carrying on.
